data.body:
Root cause confirmed (cited): scripts/amend_commit_message.py::_run reads only extract_change_id() off HEAD; compose_message() re-attaches only the Change-Id trailer; amend_head() runs `git commit --amend --file`, which replaces the message wholesale. So any Signed-off-by on HEAD that the replacement FILE omits is silently dropped while Change-Id survives. Present since the tool's introduction (13c7fe9ae1). Reproduced deterministically in a scratch repo: HEAD with 2 sign-offs + Change-Id, FILE without trailers -> after amend, Change-Id kept, both sign-offs gone.

Fix (RED->GREEN): compose_message() now also takes HEAD's sign-offs (extract_sign_offs, order-preserving, all of them) and appends them via git interpret-trailers ONLY when the stripped FILE carries no Signed-off-by of its own — a file supplying one is authoritative (nothing carried, nothing duplicated); a HEAD without one gets none invented. Change-Id semantics untouched, including the refusal when HEAD has none.

Tests added to tests/unit/test_amend_msg_change_id.py: (1) wrapper preserves both sign-offs in order where naive --amend -F loses them (negative control included), (2) FILE's own sign-off respected / not duplicated (same identity and different identity), (3) no sign-off on HEAD -> none invented. All 4 AC covered; existing 7 tests pass unmodified. Gates: make lint OK, make typecheck OK, complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0.
